newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela gasoline will not rise before new law.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela gasoline will not rise before new law.

text.p: Venezuela's subsidised domestic gasoline prices will not rise before Congress approves a new internal market law aimed at liberalising the market completely, the Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said Friday.

"It would be a contradiction to raise prices by decree when what we have proposed is market liberalisation, where competition will set the value of these products," Arrieta told journalists in the presidential Miraflores palace.
"Domestic prices will not rise until the law is approved," he added.

The government hiked prices by 450 percent last year under an economic rescue deal with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), but they have since fallen in real terms because of high inflation. The IMF deal envisaged prices rising to market levels, which the government has proposed to Congress in a new internal market law.

According to this plan, current premium grade prices of 60 bolivars per litre would rise initially to the factory gate level (currently about 80 bolivars per litre) and the free market would determine prices a year after that.
But the government proposal will have to fight off a competing plan drawn up by some congressmen which envisages more state intervention in the market.
The deputy Energy and Mines Minister has said he expects Congress to approve the new law by the end of this year.
